biography.plain_text: Nancy S. Mueller is an American entrepreneur who built Nancy's Specialty Foods, founded in 1977 and sold in 1999. A former pharmaceutical research chemist at Syntex, she developed a national frozen-food business with advice from her venture-capitalist husband, Glenn. She studied at Russell Sage College and made Palo Alto her home.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before building a national food business, Nancy S. Mueller tested whether a popular party dish could become a viable product. She investigated what customers would pay for her miniature quiches, then worked backwards to assess the economics. The range grew from bite-sized appetisers to individual and entree-sized quiches that could be heated quickly at home.

In 2015, Mueller helped create the Northern California ARCS Scholar Symposium, bringing almost 60 scholars to Silicon Valley to present their scientific research. She chaired its second edition in 2016, with an emphasis on introductions and discussion among researchers, ARCS members and guests.
